reviews.body:
Thanks for this. I checked out the branch on macOS (Python 3.11): `tests/test_templates.py` passes (53 tests), and a template with `Summarize: ${input}` now reports `input` as a variable, so the CLI no longer appends the input a second time. `$$` escapes still work.

One suggestion: since `requires-python` is `>=3.11`, `string.Template.get_identifiers()` (added in 3.11) does exactly this, covering both the `named` and `braced` groups. It also removes duplicates. That matters a bit more now: with the PR, `Greet ${name} and $name` with no `name` given prints `Missing variables: name, name` (the same thing already happens on main for `$name $name`). With `return string_template.get_identifiers()` the message is `Missing variables: name`, and all 53 template tests still pass.

comments.body:
Thanks for testing this and for the suggestion. `extract_vars` now returns `string_template.get_identifiers()`, so `Greet ${name} and $name` reports `Missing variables: name` once. A regression case covers it, and `tests/test_templates.py` passes (54 tests).

This comment was drafted with Claude Code.
